description.value: A cross-sectional structural MRI study comparing subcortical volumes in individuals with alcohol dependence only, individuals with polysubstance use disorder, and healthy controls.

spans.text: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of subcortical volumes in three groups: individuals with alcohol dependence only, individuals with polysubstance use disorder, and a comparison group of healthy controls.

value: Both ADO and PS individuals have decreased subcortical volumes compared to HC
PS individuals have increased subcortical volume compared to ADO individuals
In ADO and PS individuals, subcortical volumes negatively correlate with drinking measures and directly correlate with poor cognitive performance

spans.text: We examined the following hypotheses: (1) Both ADO and PS individuals have decreased subcortical volumes compared to HC; (2) PS individuals have increased subcortical volume compared to ADO individuals; and (3) In ADO and PS individuals, subcortical volumes negatively correlate with drinking measures and directly correlate with poor cognitive performance.

description.value: Cross-sectional study of three participant groups; alcohol-dependent participants were recruited from an inpatient alcohol treatment program and healthy controls were community recruited.

spans.text: We compared subcortical brain volume in three groups: individuals with alcohol dependence only (ADO), individuals with polysubstance use disorder (PS; all diagnosed with alcohol dependence and at least two additional substance use disorders), and healthy control participants (HC).

name.value: Healthy Controls vs. Individuals with Alcohol Dependence Only

spans.text: ##### Healthy Controls vs. Individuals with Alcohol Dependence Only

definition.value: HC had significantly greater volume in the bilateral hippocampus, right thalamus, and right nucleus accumbens compared to ADO.

value: HC had significantly greater subcortical volume in the bilateral hippocampus, right thalamus, and right nucleus accumbens compared to ADO.
Compared to healthy controls, individuals with alcohol dependence only had reduced volume in the bilateral hippocampus, right nucleus accumbens, and right thalamus.

name.value: Healthy Controls vs. Individuals with Polysubstance Use Disorder

spans.text: ##### Healthy Controls vs. Individuals with Polysubstance Use Disorder

definition.value: HC had significantly greater volume in the left and right thalamus compared to PS.

value: HC had significantly greater volume in the left and right thalamus compared to PS.
Compared to healthy controls, individuals with polysubstance use disorder had reduced volume in the bilateral thalamus.

name.value: Individuals with Alcohol Dependence Only vs. Individuals with Polysubstance Use Disorder

spans.text: ##### Individuals with Alcohol Dependence Only vs. Individuals with Polysubstance Use Disorder

definition.value: PS had significantly larger right caudate volume compared to ADO.

value: PS had significantly larger right caudate volume compared to ADO.

The right caudate was the only region that showed a significant difference between the alcohol dependent groups; its larger volume in PS may reflect a neuroprotective effect of polysubstance use or inflammation masking the effects of alcohol.

spans.text: Whole-brain high-resolution coronal structural scans were collected using a T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) pulse sequence
All subjects were scanned using a 1.5 T General Electric MRI scanner (General Electric, Milwaukee, WI) and a standard head coil.

Whole-brain high-resolution coronal structural scans were collected using a T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) pulse sequence with matrix 256 × 256 × 124, repetition time (TR) = 100 ms, echo time (TE) = 12 ms, field of view (FOV) = 24 cm, and voxel size of (0.9375 × 0.9375 × 2.0) mm 3 .
